data.title: AN2 Therapeutics, Inc. Reports Inducement Grants Under Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
AN2 Therapeutics, Inc. (), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company developing novel small molecule therapeutics derived from its boron chemistry platform, today announced it granted inducement equity awards to two newly-hired employees.

On October 19, 2026, the Compensation Committee granted inducement equity awards to two newly hired employees consisting in the aggregate of options to purchase 10,565 shares of the Company's common stock and 5,283 restricted stock units (RSUs). The options have an exercise price equal to the closing price of the Company's common stock on The Nasdaq Global Market on October 19, 2026, which was $3.37 per share.

One quarter of the non-qualified stock option (NQSO) will vest on the one-year anniversary of the Vesting Commencement Date. Thereafter, 1/48th of the NQSO will vest each month on the same day of the month as the Vesting Commencement Date. RSUs, which will vest annually over a 4-year period, are subject to continuous service with the Company.

The above-described awards were granted as a material inducement to the employee’s employment and were approved by AN2’s Compensation Committee of the board of directors in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4). The inducement awards were granted pursuant to AN2’s 2026 Employment Inducement Award Plan.

About AN2 Therapeutics

AN2 Therapeutics, Inc. is a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery and development of novel small molecule therapeutics derived from our boron chemistry platform. Our development pipeline spans hematologic diseases, infectious diseases, and oncology with three Phase 2 studies expected to be active in 2026, two preclinical candidates, as well as advanced research programs focused on targets in oncology, bone disorders, and infectious diseases. We are committed to delivering high-impact drugs to patients that address critical unmet needs and improve health outcomes.

data.title: 10-Acre Parcel Under Contract at Iron Mask Industrial Park Signals Continued Momentum in Kamloops, B.C.
data.description:
(TheNewswire)

    Growing interest in the 190-acre light industrial development highlights opportunities for businesses looking to establish or expand operations in Kamloops.

    Kamloops, B.C. – TheNewswire - October 23, 2026 – Comet Industries Ltd. (TSXV:CMU) (“Comet Industries”) is pleased to announce continued momentum at Iron Mask Industrial Park (“IMIP”), with Lot 1, a 10-acre parcel, now under contract in a proposed transaction valued at approximately $10.3 million.

    The proposed transaction marks another significant milestone for the 190-acre light industrial development and builds on the previously announced $22-million sale of a 24.36-acre parcel representing approximately 22-acres of usable land in addition to the sale of a 1.25-acre parcel. Growing interest in the industrial park reflects its appeal to businesses seeking serviced industrial land, strong transportation connections, and room to expand in Kamloops.

    “This is another exciting step forward for Iron Mask Industrial Park and a strong indication of the interest we're seeing in the development,” said Mike O'Reilly, President and CEO of Comet Industries. “We've worked hard to create a location that meets the needs of businesses looking to establish or expand their operations in Kamloops. With another major parcel under contract, we're seeing that vision continue to take shape.”

    Strategically located within Kamloops’ city limits, IMIP offers convenient access to the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1) and Coquihalla Highway (Highway 5), connecting businesses to major transportation networks throughout British Columbia and beyond. The development is designed to accommodate a wide range of light industrial uses, with water, sewer, hydro, and natural gas services at lot lines, spacious road networks for commercial trucking, and flexible parcel configurations. The park also offers convenient access to downtown Kamloops, Kamloops Airport, and both CN and CP rail yards.

    According to Blake Gozda, Senior Vice President, Industrial with Cushman & Wakefield, the development offers an attractive combination of location, infrastructure, and flexibility for businesses considering their next move.

    “What has made Iron Mask Industrial Park particularly attractive to the businesses our team has been talking to is the ability to find industrial space that meets their needs today while allowing for future growth,” said Gozda. “The combination of serviced land, transportation access, and flexible lot sizes creates a compelling opportunity for companies looking to expand in the Kamloops region.”

    With additional parcels available and options to combine lots to accommodate larger industrial operations, IMIP continues to position itself as an important part of Kamloops' future economic growth.

    “We're excited about the momentum we're building and the opportunities ahead,” added O'Reilly. “Iron Mask Industrial Park is about supporting long-term business growth and amplifying new opportunities for companies to be part of Kamloops' future.”

    Phase 1 is approximately 60% sold out. Businesses interested in exploring opportunities at Iron Mask Industrial Park are encouraged to visit www.ironmaskindustrialpark.ca or contact the sales team for information on current and future land availability.

    About Comet Industries Ltd.

    Comet Industries Ltd. was established in 1972, incorporated in British Columbia, and is listed on the TSX Venture Exchange. The company holds and develops real estate properties in British Columbia, including land in Kamloops and Nelson Island. A major initiative of the company is the Iron Mask Industrial Park project. Visit: www.cometindustries.ca | LinkedIn

data.title: Valaris Files 8K - Other Events >VAL
data.description:
Valaris Ltd. (VAL) filed a Form 8K - Other Events - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on October 23, 2026.

As previously announced, on February 9, 2026, Valaris Limited, an exempted company limited by shares incorporated under the laws of Bermuda ("Valaris"), and Transocean Ltd., a Swiss corporation ("Transocean"), entered into a Business Combination Agreement (the "Agreement"). The Agreement provides that, among other things and upon the terms and subject to the conditions thereof, Transocean will acquire all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Valaris (the "Valaris Shares") in exchange for 15.235 shares of Transocean per Valaris Share (the "Business Combination"), pursuant to a court-sanctioned scheme of Arrangement (the "Scheme of Arrangement") between Valaris and the shareholders of Valaris (the "Valaris Shareholders"), pursuant to section 99 of the Companies Act 1981 of Bermuda, as amended (the "Companies Act").

On October 14, 2026, Valaris and Transocean filed a joint definitive proxy statement on Schedule 14A with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the "Proxy Statement") in connection with the (i) special court-ordered meeting of Valaris (the "Valaris Court Meeting"), at which the Valaris Shareholders will vote on, among other matters related to the Business Combination, the Scheme of Arrangement and (ii) extraordinary general meeting (the "Transocean Meeting") of shareholders of Transocean (the "Transocean Shareholders") at which the Transocean Shareholders will vote on certain matters related to the Business Combination. Both the Valaris Court Meeting and the Transocean Meeting are scheduled to be held on November 24, 2026.

Subject to approval by the Valaris Shareholders of the Scheme of Arrangement at the Valaris Court Meeting and approval by the Transocean Shareholders of the requisite matters related to the Business Combination at the Transocean Meeting, in accordance with the Agreement Valaris will make an application to the Supreme Court of Bermuda (the "Bermuda Court"), for an order sanctioning the Scheme of Arrangement in accordance with section 99 of the Companies Act (the "Sanction Hearing").

The Sanction Hearing has been scheduled to be held on Thursday, November 26, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Bermuda time) at Commercial Court, 2nd Floor, Government Administration Building, 30 Parliament Street, Hamilton HM12, Bermuda. Valaris Shareholders of record may appear in person or by counsel at the Sanction Hearing.

If the Bermuda Court grants the sanction order and sanctions the Scheme of Arrangement at the Sanction Hearing, Valaris anticipates that (i) all conditions to the consummation of the Business Combination will be satisfied and (ii) the Business Combination will be consummated on or about December 1, 2026.

River City Bank's third-quarter net income jumped 55% year over year to $30.6 million, driven largely by a $17.1 million mark-to-market gain on undesignated interest rate swaps. The gain resulted from rising U.S. Treasury rates during the quarter. Management said it doesn't view the MTM fluctuations as indicative of core operating performance, noting that about 16% of the bank's interest rate swaps remain undesignated. Excluding the swap gain, adjusted EPS came in at $1.29, compared with $1.43 in the year-ago period.

data.title: River City Bank's Deposit and Loan Growth Fuel 15% Jump in Core Pretax Earnings — Company Talk
data.description:
River City Bank's core pre-tax, pre-provision income rose 15% to $29.3 million in the third quarter from the prior quarter, supported by continued loan and deposit expansion. data.title: Fujitsu implements multi-AI agent infrastructure to enhance product information management for MISUMI Group
data.description:
KAWASAKI, Japan, Oct 23, 2026 - (JCN Newswire) - Fujitsu Limited today announced that it has implemented a multi-AI agent infrastructure for the product information management business of MISUMI Group Inc. (MISUMI). Building on the operation platform of its business model Uvance[1], Fujitsu leveraged "Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS"[2] to establish a system that supports the entire process, from data collection and pre-processing to AI-driven generation, evaluation, and final human verification. MISUMI began operating this new workflow in October.

This workflow targets tens of thousands of products listed on MISUMI's e-commerce site. By creating an operational model where humans and AI collaborate, the project aims to improve both the efficiency and quality of product information management.

The platform was built in approximately 2.5 months. This rapid deployment was achieved through an agile development process, where Fujitsu's Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) worked closely with MISUMI's business personnel to integrate professional operational judgment criteria and verification methods directly into the AI agents.

Background

As MISUMI has expanded its product offerings, the volume of data requiring registration, including product category classifications and technical specifications, has grown substantially. Registering new products and series typically required manual, time-consuming processes across multiple internal and external systems. These manual dependencies created bottlenecks, delaying product launches on the e-commerce site and presenting challenges in maintaining data consistency and quality. To address these issues, Fujitsu is leveraging Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS to transform the business processes through AI integration.

Project Highlights

1. Rapid implementation

Fujitsu quickly established a data utilization foundation and AI execution environment by leveraging Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS. In addition, Fujitsu's Forward Deployed Engineers (FDE) worked in close cooperation with business personnel at MISUMI to incorporate their expertise, such as operational judgment criteria and verification methods, into the AI agents. The team also built a workflow that integrates a confirmation and approval process by human operators. Through this agile development approach, the multi-AI agent platform was successfully applied to actual business operations in just 2.5 months after the project began.

2. Quality enhancement through AI collaboration

The workflow utilizes nine AI agents, each with distinct roles such as generating series names, suggesting categories, extracting specifications, and checking for restricted characters. These agents mutually evaluate the validity of their outputs, while final human approval ensures accuracy and consistency across the catalog.

3. Focus on high-value operations

Automating routine registration and verification tasks significantly reduces the administrative burden on staff. This allows employees to shift their focus toward higher-value activities, such as strategic decision-making and business process improvements.

Future Plans

Fujitsu will continue to collaborate with MISUMI to gradually expand the scope of the developed data models and AI-driven workflows. The next phases will include end-to-end management from initial product data ingestion from suppliers to master data management, with the goal of further automating the entire workflow through integration with peripheral systems. Fujitsu remains committed to supporting business transformation in the manufacturing sector through its Uvance model, driving faster time-to-market and increased industrial competitiveness.

[1] Uvance:

A business model committed to realizing customer transformation and creating social value in an era where AI is reshaping the world.

[2] Fujitsu Data Intelligence PaaS:

A platform composed of the "Fujitsu Kozuchi" AI platform; "Fujitsu Track and Trust," which enables cross-enterprise and cross-industry data collaboration and traceability through technologies including blockchain; and data platforms such as "Palantir Foundry" and "Microsoft Azure." (C) Palantir Technologies Inc.

About Fujitsu

Fujitsu's purpose is to make the world more sustainable by building trust in society through innovation. As the digital transformation partner of choice for customers around the globe, our 100,000 employees work to resolve some of the greatest challenges facing humanity. Our range of services and solutions draw on five key technologies: AI, Computing, Networks, Data & Security, and Converging Technologies, which we bring together to deliver sustainability transformation. Fujitsu Limited (TSE:6702) reported consolidated revenues of 3.5 trillion yen (US$23 billion) for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026 and remains the top digital services company in Japan by market share. data.title: Defensive-led market breadth is a warning sign, not a win - Carson
data.description:
Carson Group is warning investors that the long-awaited expansion in market breadth may have arrived with a painful catch—it's being driven by defensive sectors while AI stocks are in freefall.

On Thursday, 324 of 500 S&P 500 companies increased, with the median stock climbing 1.09%, Carson noted in a blog post published Friday. Yet the S&P 500 itself fell 1.36%, technology plunged 3.3%, and the Goldman Sachs Broad AI Index dropped 6.01%. Nine of 11 sectors beat the index, with defensive plays—staples , utilities , and health care —leading the way.

The shift has been dramatic. On June 22, AI stocks were outperforming non-AI stocks by 49 percentage points year-to-date. That lead has collapsed to just 4.8 points.

Through Thursday, non-AI stocks have outperformed AI by over 28 percentage points in the second half of 2026.

The concentration problem is acute. Technology alone represents 38% of the S&P 500, and adding Alphabet , Meta , Amazon , and Tesla pushes AI-linked exposure past 51%, Carson said. In the first half of 2026, when the S&P 500 returned 10.2%, the AI basket contributed 75% of that gain despite averaging only 37% of index weight.

That dynamic has reversed. In the second half, the AI basket—now 39% of the index—has subtracted 1.7 percentage points from S&P 500 returns, while non-AI stocks contributed 4.2 points.

Carson pointed out that that rotation marked the end of the late 1990s tech bubble and warned that if the current pattern persists, it could signal the end of both the AI wave and the broader bull market.

data.title: Hilltop Holdings 3Q 2026: Revenue $309.5M, EPS $0.44— 10-Q Summary
data.description:
Hilltop Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $309.5 million, down 6.3% from a year earlier, as lower broker-dealer and mortgage income weighed on results. Net income attributable to Hilltop fell 45.7% to $24.9 million, while diluted EPS declined to $0.44 from $0.74.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue was $309.5M, compared with $330.2M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (6.3%).
  • Net income attributable to Hilltop was $24.9M, compared with $45.8M in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (45.7%).
  • Diluted EPS was $0.44, compared with $0.74 in the prior-year quarter; YoY change (40.5%).

Business Highlights

  • Nine-month banking net interest income rose 7%, as lower deposit costs and higher loan volumes offset lower yields on bank deposits.
  • Nine-month broker-dealer revenue declined 2%, primarily due to weaker structured finance activity; wealth management fees and commissions increased.
  • Nine-month mortgage loan volume grew 2.5%, and refinancing rose to 17.7% of originations. Higher interest rates and weaker production margins contributed to larger mortgage losses.
  • Potential problem loans increased to $204.5 million, while non-accrual loans declined. The company cited elevated risks in some real estate and consumer sectors.
  • Hilltop expects mortgage production to decline in the fourth quarter amid higher rates and seasonal weakness, and continues cost-saving efforts at PrimeLending.

Original SEC Filing: Hilltop Holdings Inc. [ HTH ] - 10-Q - Oct. 23, 2026

data.title: Colombia's Ecopetrol sees Q3 profit drop to up to $1.57 billion
data.description:
Colombian state-run energy company Ecopetrol estimated its third-quarter net profit at 4 trillion to 5 trillion pesos ($1.26 billion to $1.57 billion), the company said on Friday, a decline from the 6.06 trillion pesos ($1.90 billion) it posted in the second quarter.

  • Total revenue for July-September quarter was estimated at 33 trillion to 36 trillion pesos ($10.36 billion to $11.30 billion), Ecopetrol said.

  • Third-quarter production is estimated to have reached between 740,000 to 750,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day (bpd), an increase from the 705,800 bpd the company reported in the second quarter.

  • In September Ecopetrol appointed businessman Joaquin Gutierrez as its chief executive, giving one of the country's most important corporate jobs to a close presidential ally with no known background in the energy sector.

  • Colombia's right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella, who took office in August, has promised to strengthen Ecopetrol, boost reserves and secure domestic oil and gas supply, including through fracking.

  • Ecopetrol is majority state-controlled and Colombia's largest company, generating most of the South American country's oil production.

  • The company owns the two main refineries and most of the country's oil and product pipeline network.

($1 = 3.185,01 pesos)
